chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz narrated to us from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (blessings be upon him and his family) passed by a group of people who were lifting a boulder competitively. He said: What is this? They said: Through this, we determine who is strongest among us. So he said: Shall I not inform you who is truly strongest among you? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: The strongest among you is he who, when he is pleased, his pleasure does not lead him into sin or falsehood; when he is discontented, his discontentment does not lead him from speaking the truth; and when he has power, he does not take that which is not rightfully his.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about true strength and self-control?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) encountered people testing physical strength by lifting boulders. He redefined true strength in three dimensions: emotional control when pleased (not being led to sin by happiness), emotional control when angry (not abandoning truth due to frustration), and moral restraint when powerful (not abusing one's position). This teaching transforms the concept of strength from mere physical capability to comprehensive moral character, making self-mastery the highest form of power.
